title: Ensure 'mysqld' is Not Started With '--skip-grant-tables'
description: This option causes mysqld to start without using the privilege system. Counts enabled skip-grant-tables settings in the server option groups and on the running server command line.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.5 Ensure 'mysqld' is Not Started With '--skip-grant-tables'

audit.command:
c=$(my_print_defaults mysqld 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(ps -eo comm=,args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=$( { printf '%s
' "$c"; printf '%s
' "$p" | awk '$1=="mysqld"||$1=="mariadbd"' | tr ' ' '
'; } | grep -Eic '^--skip[-_]grant[-_]tables(=(1|on|true|yes))?$' ); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove skip-grant-tables (and skip_grant_tables) from the option files or set skip-grant-tables = FALSE, remove it from the start-up command line, and restart MySQL.

title: Ensure Passwords are Set for All MySQL Accounts
description: Blank passwords allow a user to login without using a password. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.3 Ensure Passwords are Set for All MySQL Accounts

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE (plugin IN ('sha256_password', 'caching_sha2_password') AND LENGTH(authentication_string) = 0) OR (plugin IN ('mysql_native_password', 'mysql_old_password', '') AND (authentication_string IS NULL OR LENGTH(authentication_string) = 0))" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER <user>@<host> IDENTIFIED BY RANDOM PASSWORD PASSWORD EXPIRE; for each account returned, and hand the temporary password over securely.

title: Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for MySQL Daemon/Service
description: As with any service installed on a host, it can be provided with its own user context. Providing a dedicated user to the service provides the ability to precisely constrain the service within the larger host context. Passes when the running mysqld process does not run as root (the benchmark expects the mysql account).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.2 Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for MySQL Daemon/Service

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user:32=,comm= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2=="mysqld"||$2=="mariadbd"{n++; if($1=="root")r++} END{if(!n)print "not-running"; else if(r)print "runs-as-root"; else print "compliant"}'

remediation.command: Run MySQL under a dedicated unprivileged account (normally mysql, no sudo rights, shell /bin/false): groupadd -r mysql; useradd -r -M -g mysql -d /var/lib/mysql -s /bin/false mysql; set user=mysql under [mysqld] or User=mysql in the systemd unit, then restart.

title: Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions
description: MySQL supports multiple protocols of TLS. The higher the version the stronger the security and/or better the performance. Also review performance_schema.status_by_thread (Ssl_version) for clients still negotiating old versions. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.15 Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(FIND_IN_SET('TLSv1', @@global.tls_version) = 0 AND FIND_IN_SET('TLSv1.1', @@global.tls_version) = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set tls_version=TLSv1.3 (or TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3) under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf) (or SET PERSIST tls_version then ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS), then restart MySQL.

title: Ensure 'datadir' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: The data directory is the location of the MySQL databases. Expects drwxr-x--- mysql:mysql (0700 also accepted); run as root on the database host. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.1 Ensure 'datadir' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$d" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$s" in "750 mysql mysql"|"700 mysql mysql") echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

title: Ensure SSL Key Files Have Appropriate Permissions
description: When configured to use SSL/TLS, MySQL relies on Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) key files, which are stored on the host's filesystem. These SSL key files are subject to the host's permissions and ownership structure. Every file named by an ssl_ca/ssl_cert/ssl_key/ssl_crl variable must be -r-------- mysql:mysql (directories in ssl_capath/ssl_crlpath are skipped). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.7 Ensure SSL Key Files Have Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; l=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) REGEXP '^.*ssl_(ca|capath|cert|crl|crlpath|key)\$' AND VARIABLE_VALUE <> ''" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=0; for f in $l; do case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; [ -f "$f" ] || continue; [ "$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$f")" = "400 mysql mysql" ] || n=$((n+1)); done; [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chown mysql:mysql <ssl_file> && chmod 400 <ssl_file> for every ssl_ca/ssl_cert/ssl_key/ssl_crl file in use.

title: Ensure Plugin Directory Has Appropriate Permissions
description: The plugin directory is the location of the MySQL plugins. Plugins are storage engines or user defined functions (UDFs). Expects plugin_dir mode 550 or 554. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.8 Ensure Plugin Directory Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; p=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.plugin_dir, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; m=$(stat -c %a "$p" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$m" in 550|554) echo compliant ;; *) echo "mode $m" ;; esac

remediation.command: chmod 550 <plugin_dir> (or 554) && chown mysql:mysql <plugin_dir>; the server must not be able to write to it.

title: Ensure the Latest Security Patches are Applied
description: Periodically, updates to MySQL server are released to resolve bugs, mitigate vulnerabilities, and provide new features. It is recommended that MySQL installations are up to date with the latest security updates.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1 Ensure the Latest Security Patches are Applied

audit.command: Run SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name LIKE 'version'; and compare with the latest release and security announcements from Oracle (Critical Patch Updates) and your OS vendor. An outdated release is a fail.

remediation.command: Upgrade MySQL to the latest release of the installed series with the package manager during a maintenance window and run the upgrade steps for the release.

title: Ensure Only Administrative Users Have Full Database Access
description: The mysql.user, mysql.db, and other mysql tables ending in _priv list a variety of privileges that can be granted (or denied) to MySQL users. Some of the privileges of concern include: Select_priv, Insert_priv, Update_priv, Delete_priv, Drop_priv, and so on.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.1 Ensure Only Administrative Users Have Full Database Access

audit.command: Run SELECT * FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE grantee NOT LIKE ('\'mysql.%localhost\''); and ensure all returned users are administrative users with the minimal privileges required.

remediation.command: REVOKE unnecessary privileges (e.g. REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>';) and GRANT only database-level privileges that are needed.

title: Ensure 'FILE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The FILE privilege is used to allow or disallow a user from reading and writing files on the server host. Any user with the FILE right granted has the ability to: ; Read files from the local file system that are readable by the MySQL server (this includes world-readable files). ; Write files to the local file system where the MySQL server has write access.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.2 Ensure 'FILE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'FILE'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE FILE ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The SUPER privilege is a powerful and far-reaching privilege and should not be granted lightly. In MySQL 8.0, SUPER is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of MySQL. The SUPER privilege shown in the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES table governs the use of a variety of MySQL features.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.4 Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'SUPER'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The CREATE USER privilege governs the right of a given user to add or remove users, change existing users' names, or revoke existing users' privileges.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.6 Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'CREATE USER'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE CREATE USER ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'GRANT OPTION' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The GRANT OPTION privilege exists in different contexts (mysql.user, mysql.db) for the purpose of governing the ability of a privileged user to manipulate the privileges of other users.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.7 Ensure 'GRANT OPTION' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT DISTINCT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE IS_GRANTABLE = 'YES'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE GRANT OPTION ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'log-raw' is Set to 'OFF'
description: The log-raw MySQL option determines whether passwords are rewritten by the server so as not to appear in log files as plain text. If log-raw is enabled, then passwords are written to the various log files (general query log, slow query log, and binary log) in plain text. Reads the effective log_raw value (OFF is also the default); also ensure no log-raw = ON remains in my.cnf. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 6.4 Ensure 'log-raw' is Set to 'OFF'

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.log_raw = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST log_raw = OFF"

title: Ensure your authentication_policy is Set to a Secure Option
description: Define your authentication policy by setting the mysql system variable authentication_policy. The default value of authentication_policy is '*,,'. This means that factor 1 is required in account definitions and can use any authentication plugin (with caching_sha2_password being the default), and that factors 2 and 3 are optional and each can use any authentication plugin. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.1 Ensure your authentication_policy is Set to a Secure Option

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.authentication_policy NOT LIKE '%mysql_native_password%', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set authentication_policy (e.g. '*,,' or 'caching_sha2_password,,') without mysql_native_password, then migrate accounts: SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE plugin = 'mysql_native_password'; ALTER USER <user> IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY RANDOM PASSWORD PASSWORD EXPIRE;

title: Ensure Passwords are Not Stored in the Global Configuration
description: The [client] section of the MySQL configuration file allows setting a user and password to be used. Verify the password option is not used in the global configuration file (my.cnf). Reads the [client] groups of /etc/my.cnf and /etc/mysql/my.cnf (including !include files) with my_print_defaults; per-user ~/.my.cnf files are not global and are ignored.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.2 Ensure Passwords are Not Stored in the Global Configuration

audit.command: n=0; found=0; for c in /etc/my.cnf /etc/mysql/my.cnf; do [ -f "$c" ] || continue; found=1; o=$(my_print_defaults --defaults-file="$c" client 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=$((n + $(printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -c '^--password'))); done; [ "$found" -eq 1 ] || exit 1; echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove password= from the [client] section of the global option files; use mysql_config_editor (~/.mylogin.cnf) or a per-user ~/.my.cnf with mode 0600 instead.

title: Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place
description: Password complexity includes password characteristics such as length, case, numerical, and character sets. Requires the validate_password component with length >= 14, check_user_name ON and policy STRONG (the dictionary file contents are not checked). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.5 Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.component WHERE component_urn LIKE '%validate_password') > 0 AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'validate_password.length') >= 14 AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'validate_password.check_user_name') = 'ON' AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'validate_password.policy') = 'STRONG', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: INSTALL COMPONENT 'file://component_validate_password'; SET PERSIST validate_password.length = 14; SET PERSIST validate_password.check_user_name = ON; SET PERSIST validate_password.policy = STRONG; SET PERSIST validate_password.dictionary_file = '<dictionary file>'; then change passwords that equal the user name.

title: Ensure No Anonymous Accounts Exist
description: Anonymous accounts are users with empty usernames (''). Anonymous accounts have no passwords, so anyone can use them to connect to the MySQL server. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.7 Ensure No Anonymous Accounts Exist

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE user = ''" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: DROP USER ''@'<host>'; for each anonymous account (or run mysql_secure_installation).

title: Ensure 'require_secure_transport' is Set to 'ON'
description: All network traffic must use SSL/TLS when traveling over untrusted networks. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 8.1 Ensure 'require_secure_transport' is Set to 'ON'

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.require_secure_transport = 1, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Configure TLS certificates, confirm all clients connect with TLS, then SET PERSIST require_secure_transport = ON;

title: Ensure 'ssl_type' is Set to 'ANY', 'X509', or 'SPECIFIED' for All Remote Users
description: All network traffic must use SSL/TLS when traveling over untrusted networks. SSL/TLS should be enforced on a per-user basis for users which enter the system through the network. Counts remote accounts whose ssl_type is not ANY, X509 or SPECIFIED. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 8.2 Ensure 'ssl_type' is Set to 'ANY', 'X509', or 'SPECIFIED' for All Remote Users

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE host NOT IN ('::1', '127.0.0.1', 'localhost') AND ssl_type NOT IN ('ANY', 'X509', 'SPECIFIED')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' REQUIRE X509; (or REQUIRE SSL / ISSUER / SUBJECT) for every remote account listed by SELECT user, host, ssl_type FROM mysql.user WHERE host NOT IN ('::1','127.0.0.1','localhost');

title: Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured
description: The replication traffic between servers should be secured. Security measures should include ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of the traffic, and performing mutual authentication between the servers before performing replication.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 9.1 Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured

audit.command: Check that replication traffic uses a private network, a VPN, SSL/TLS or an SSH tunnel for confidentiality, integrity and mutual server authentication.

remediation.command: Secure replication with TLS (CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_SSL=1, SOURCE_SSL_CA=... and REQUIRE SSL/X509 for the replication account) or a private network/VPN.

title: Ensure 'SOURCE_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT' is Set to 'YES' or '1'
description: In the MySQL REPLICA (SLAVE is deprecated as of 8.0.22) context the setting SOURCE_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT (MASTER_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT is deprecated as of 8.0.22) indicates whether the REPLICA should verify the SOURCE's certificate. This configuration item may be set to Yes or No, and unless SSL has been enabled on the REPLICA, the value will be ignored. Counts replication channels that do not verify the source certificate; passes on servers that are not replicas. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 9.2 Ensure 'SOURCE_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT' is Set to 'YES' or '1'

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.slave_master_info WHERE Ssl_verify_server_cert <> 1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: STOP REPLICA; CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT = 1; START REPLICA;

title: Ensure 'super_priv' is Not Set to 'Y' for Replication Users
description: The SUPER privilege found in the mysql.user table governs the use of a variety of MySQL features. These features include, CHANGE MASTER TO, KILL, mysqladmin kill option, PURGE BINARY LOGS, SET GLOBAL, mysqladmin debug option, logging control, and more. Treats every account other than root holding REPLICATION SLAVE as a replication user and counts those that also hold SUPER. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 9.3 Ensure 'super_priv' is Not Set to 'Y' for Replication Users

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE Repl_slave_priv = 'Y' AND Super_priv = 'Y' AND user NOT IN ('root')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM '<repl user>'@'<host>'; (grant REPLICATION_SLAVE_ADMIN instead if MySQL Shell ReplicaSet administration needs it).

title: Ensure All Group Replication Traffic is Secured
description: MySQL Group communication connections and distributed recovery connections can be secured using SSL.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 10.1 Ensure All Group Replication Traffic is Secured

audit.command: In MySQL Shell run dba.getCluster().status() and check ssl is not DISABLED, or run SELECT @@group_replication_ssl_mode; DISABLED is a finding; REQUIRED, VERIFY_CA or VERIFY_IDENTITY mean TLS is enforced. Also check group_replication_recovery_use_ssl = ON.

remediation.command: Create the cluster with memberSslMode REQUIRED/VERIFY_IDENTITY (dba.createCluster(name, {memberSslMode: 'VERIFY_IDENTITY'})) or set group_replication_ssl_mode=REQUIRED and group_replication_recovery_use_ssl=ON on every member.

title: Verify That the MYSQL_PWD Environment Variable is Not in Use
description: MySQL can read a default database password from an environment variable called MYSQL_PWD. Avoiding use of this environment variable can better safeguard the confidentiality of MySQL credentials. Run as root; counts processes whose environment contains MYSQL_PWD (including the scanner itself if it was given MYSQL_PWD).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.4 Verify That the MYSQL_PWD Environment Variable is Not in Use

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -lsaz '^MYSQL_PWD=' /proc/[0-9]*/environ 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Find the processes (grep -lsaz ^MYSQL_PWD= /proc/*/environ) and change the users/scripts that export MYSQL_PWD to use an option file readable only by the user, mysql_config_editor or certificate-based authentication.

title: Ensure Interactive Login is Disabled
description: When created, the MySQL user may have interactive access to the operating system, which means that the MySQL user could login to the host as any other user would. Checks that the mysql account has /bin/false or nologin as its shell.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.5 Ensure Interactive Login is Disabled

audit.command: out=$(getent passwd mysql 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; s=${out##*:}; case "$s" in /bin/false|/usr/bin/false|/sbin/nologin|/usr/sbin/nologin) echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

remediation.command: usermod -s /bin/false mysql

title: Verify That 'MYSQL_PWD' is Not Set in Users' Profiles
description: MySQL can read a default database password from an environment variable called MYSQL_PWD. Run as root; counts Bash login scripts in /home/*, /root and /etc/environment that mention MYSQL_PWD.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.6 Verify That 'MYSQL_PWD' is Not Set in Users' Profiles

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -ls MYSQL_PWD /home/*/.bashrc /home/*/.profile /home/*/.bash_profile /root/.bashrc /root/.profile /root/.bash_profile /etc/environment 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$n"

remediation.guidance: Remove MYSQL_PWD from the listed login scripts and use a protected option file (~/.my.cnf, mode 0600) or mysql_config_editor instead.

title: Backup Policy in Place
description: A backup policy should be in place.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1 Backup Policy in Place

audit.command: Check that a backup schedule exists (crontab -l for the backup user, systemd timers or the backup tool scheduler) covering all databases.

remediation.command: Define and schedule regular full and incremental backups (mysqldump/MySQL Shell dump utilities/MySQL Enterprise Backup), e.g. via cron or systemd timers.

title: Verify Backups are Good
description: Backups should be validated on a regular basis.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.2 Verify Backups are Good

audit.command: Check reports of backup validation tests: backups must be restored regularly to a test system and verified.

remediation.command: Implement a regular restore test of backups and keep the validation reports.

title: Secure Backup Credentials
description: A database user with the least amount of privileges required to perform backup is needed. The credentials for this user should be protected. The password, certificate, and any other credentials should be protected.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.3 Secure Backup Credentials

audit.command: Check permissions of files containing backup passwords and/or SSL keys (ls -l on option files and key files used by backup jobs); they must be readable only by the backup account.

remediation.command: chmod 600 the files holding backup credentials/keys and chown them to the backup user; prefer an option file over passwords on the command line.

title: Point-in-Time Recovery
description: With binlogs it is possible to implement point-in-time recovery. This makes it possible to restore the changes between the last full backup and the point-in-time. Enabling binlogs is not sufficient. The binlogs need to be backed up to separate media. The restore procedure should be created and tested. Passes when binary logging is enabled and binlog_expire_logs_seconds is not 0. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.4 Point-in-Time Recovery

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.log_bin = 1 AND @@global.binlog_expire_logs_seconds <> 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set log_bin=<path> and binlog_expire_logs_seconds=<retention seconds, not 0> under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf), then create and test a point-in-time restore procedure, then restart MySQL.

title: Disaster Recovery (DR) Plan
description: A disaster recovery plan should be created. MySQL Cluster (group replication), MySQL Replica Sets (asynchronous replication) or both may be used. A replica in a different data center and offsite backups may be used. There should be information regarding the Recovery Time Objective (RTO), i.e., how long recovery will take, and if the recovery site has the same capacity.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.5 Disaster Recovery (DR) Plan

audit.command: Check that a documented disaster recovery plan exists (e.g. a replica in another data center or offsite backups), including recovery time objectives and tested procedures.

remediation.command: Create and test a disaster recovery plan (offsite backups, replicas in a separate location, documented restore steps).

title: Ensure Binary and Relay Logs are Encrypted
description: The binlog_encryption system variable may be used to configure encryption of the binary and relay logs. This may be configured to ON even if binary logging is not enabled in order to encrypt relay log files. Requires a keyring component/plugin to be loaded before it can be enabled. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.1 Ensure Binary and Relay Logs are Encrypted

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.binlog_encryption = 1, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST binlog_encryption = ON"

title: Do Not Specify Passwords in the Command Line
description: When a command is executed on the command line, for example mysql -u admin -p password or mysqlsh -u admin -p password, the password may be visible in the user's shell/command history or in the process list.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.4 Do Not Specify Passwords in the Command Line

audit.command: Check the process list (ps -ef) and shell histories for mysql/mysqldump invocations with -p<password> or --password=<password>. Any visible password is a fail.

remediation.command: Use -p without a value (prompt), an option file with mode 0600 or mysql_config_editor login paths instead of passwords on the command line, and clear exposed history entries.

title: Ensure Non-Default, Unique Cryptographic Material is in Use
description: The cryptographic material used by MySQL, such as digital certificates and encryption keys, should be used only for MySQL and only for one instance. Default cryptographic material should not be used since it is not unique to the instance.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.6 Ensure Non-Default, Unique Cryptographic Material is in Use

audit.command: Review all cryptographic material: openssl x509 -in <datadir or ssl_cert>/server-cert.pem -subject -noout | grep Auto_Generated_Server_Certificate. Any output (auto-generated cert) or material shared with other instances/purposes is a finding.

remediation.command: Issue a unique certificate and key from your CA for this instance, set ssl_cert/ssl_key/ssl_ca under [mysqld], and restart or run ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS.

title: Ensure 'password_lifetime' is Less Than or Equal to '365'
description: Password expiration provides users with a unique time bounded password lifetime. Fails when default_password_lifetime exceeds 365 or any account overrides it with 0 (never) or more than 365 days (fix those with ALTER USER ... PASSWORD EXPIRE INTERVAL 365 DAY). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.7 Ensure 'password_lifetime' is Less Than or Equal to '365'

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(IFNULL(@@global.default_password_lifetime, 0) <= 365 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE password_lifetime = 0 OR password_lifetime > 365) = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST default_password_lifetime = 365"

title: Ensure Password Resets Require Strong Passwords
description: Disabling password reuse, enforcing password strength, and denying reuse can be implemented to prevent successful usage of stolen or previously guessed passwords by malicious users. Restricted accounts using passwords on the basis of the number of password changes and length ensure a password cannot be chosen from a specified number of the most recent passwords. Requires password_history >= 5 and password_reuse_interval >= 365. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.8 Ensure Password Resets Require Strong Passwords

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.password_history >= 5 AND @@global.password_reuse_interval >= 365, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST password_history = 5; SET PERSIST password_reuse_interval = 365"

title: Lock Out Accounts if Not Currently in Use
description: If users with accounts will not be using their account for some time, to reduce the risk of attacks or inappropriate account usage or if suspicions exist that an account might be under attack, disabling the account will secure it and once it's ready to resume use it can easily be re-enabled.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.11 Lock Out Accounts if Not Currently in Use

audit.command: Review lock status: SELECT user, host, account_locked FROM mysql.user; Accounts not in use and MySQL reserved accounts must show account_locked = Y.

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' ACCOUNT LOCK; for each unused account (ACCOUNT UNLOCK when needed again).

title: Ensure Socket Peer-Credential Authentication is Used Appropriately
description: The server-side auth_socket authentication plugin, authenticates clients that connect to the MySQL server from the local host through the Unix socket file. Users authenticated by the auth_socket need not specify a password when connecting to the server.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.13 Ensure Socket Peer-Credential Authentication is Used Appropriately

audit.command: Run SELECT PLUGIN_NAME, PLUGIN_STATUS FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_NAME LIKE 'auth%'; and SELECT user, host, plugin FROM mysql.user WHERE plugin = 'auth_socket'; If the plugin is enabled but not allowed, a host is not localhost or an unauthorized user is listed, this is a fail.

remediation.command: Drop or re-authenticate unauthorized auth_socket users (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password ...), or remove the plugin (UNINSTALL PLUGIN auth_socket / remove plugin-load-add) if not allowed.

title: Ensure MySQL is Bound to an IP Address
description: By default, the MySQL server accepts TCP/IP connections from MySQL user accounts on all server host IPv6 and IPv4 interfaces. You can make this configuration more restrictive by setting the bind_address configuration option to a specific IPv4 or IPv6 address so that the server only accepts TCP/IP connections on that address. Fails when bind_address is empty, '*', '::' or '0.0.0.0' (all interfaces). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.14 Ensure MySQL is Bound to an IP Address

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(IFNULL(@@global.bind_address, '') NOT IN ('', '*', '::', '0.0.0.0'), 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set bind_address=<specific IP> under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf), then restart MySQL.

title: Require Client-Side Certificates (X.509)
description: Client-side certificates may be used as proof of identity as well as to encrypt data in transit. Counts non-reserved accounts that do not require a client certificate (ssl_type X509 or SPECIFIED). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.16 Require Client-Side Certificates (X.509)

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.sys') AND ssl_type NOT IN ('X509', 'SPECIFIED')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' REQUIRE X509; for each account; clients then connect with --ssl-cert, --ssl-key and --ssl-ca.

title: Ensure Only Approved Ciphers are Used
description: MySQL supports multiple encryption ciphers. Ciphers can vary in strength, speed and overhead. Expects exactly the benchmark values ssl_cipher = ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and tls_ciphersuites = TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (the ECDSA cipher needs an ECDSA server certificate). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.17 Ensure Only Approved Ciphers are Used

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.ssl_cipher = 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' AND @@global.tls_ciphersuites = 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST ssl_cipher = 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256'; SET PERSIST tls_ciphersuites = 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384'; ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS"

title: Implement Connection Delays to Limit Failed Login Attempts
description: MySQL Server can enable administrators to introduce an increasing delay in server response to clients after a certain number of consecutive failed connection attempts. Requires both connection_control plugins ACTIVE, threshold >= 5, min delay >= 60000 ms, max delay >= 1920000 ms, and FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS configured on every unlocked non-reserved account (the benchmark uses 12). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.18 Implement Connection Delays to Limit Failed Login Attempts

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_NAME IN ('CONNECTION_CONTROL','CONNECTION_CONTROL_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS') AND PLUGIN_STATUS = 'ACTIVE') = 2 AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'connection_control_failed_connections_threshold') >= 5 AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'connection_control_min_connection_delay') >= 60000 AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'connection_control_max_connection_delay') >= 1920000 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema','mysql.session','mysql.sys') AND account_locked = 'N' AND IFNULL(JSON_EXTRACT(user_attributes, '\$.Password_locking.failed_login_attempts'), 0) = 0) = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Add under [mysqld]: plugin-load-add=connection_control.so, connection-control=FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT, connection-control-failed-login-attempts=FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT, connection_control_failed_connections_threshold=5, connection_control_min_connection_delay=60000, connection_control_max_connection_delay=1920000; restart, then ALTER USER <user> FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS 12 PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME UNBOUNDED; for each account.

title: Ensure FIPS 140-2 OpenSSL Cryptography Is Used
description: Install, configure, and use OpenSSL on a platform that has a NIST certified FIPS 140-2 installation of OpenSSL. This provides MySQL instances the ability to generate and validate cryptographic hashes to protect unclassified information requiring confidentiality and cryptographic protection, in accordance with the data owner's requirements.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.19 Ensure FIPS 140-2 OpenSSL Cryptography Is Used

audit.command: FIPS mode requires MySQL built against a FIPS-certified OpenSSL 3.0 with the FIPS provider installed and the OS in FIPS mode (cat /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled = 1). In MySQL 8.4 check that the OpenSSL configuration activates the fips provider (openssl list -providers) and that mysqld logs no FIPS errors at start-up.

remediation.command: Enable OS FIPS mode (e.g. fips-mode-setup --enable on RHEL), install the OpenSSL 3 FIPS provider, configure OpenSSL to load it, and restart MySQL.

title: Ensure 'log_bin_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions
description: MySQL can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log, general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Fails when any <log_bin_basename>.* file grants other users access, is executable or is not owned by mysql:mysql (benchmark: -rw-rw---- mysql mysql); passes when binary logging is off. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.2 Ensure 'log_bin_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.log_bin_basename, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$b" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; case "$b" in /*) ;; *) b="$d/${b#./}" ;; esac; [ -d "$(dirname "$b")" ] || exit 1; n=$(find "$(dirname "$b")" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$(basename "$b").*" \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \) | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chmod 660 <log_bin_basename>.* && chown mysql:mysql <log_bin_basename>.*

title: Ensure 'log_error' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MySQL can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log, general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Expects the error log file (relative paths resolve to datadir) to be -rw------- mysql:mysql; logging to stderr only fails (see 6.1). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.3 Ensure 'log_error' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; f=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.log_error, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$f" in ""|stderr|*stderr.err) echo "no log file"; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$s" in "600 mysql mysql") echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

remediation.command: chmod 600 <log_error> && chown mysql:mysql <log_error>

title: Ensure 'slow_query_log' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MySQL can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log, general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Passes when the slow query log is off; otherwise the file must not be accessible to other users, executable, or owned by anyone but mysql:mysql. Remove old slow log files manually. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.4 Ensure 'slow_query_log' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; on=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.slow_query_log + 0, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ "$on" = 0 ] && { echo compliant; exit 0; }; f=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.slow_query_log_file, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; [ -f "$f" ] || exit 1; [ -z "$(find "$f" -maxdepth 0 \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \))" ] && echo compliant || echo "bad permissions on $f"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST slow_query_log = OFF"

title: Ensure 'relay_log_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions
description: MySQL can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log (which can be encrypted), general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Fails when any <relay_log_basename>.* file grants other users access, is executable or is not owned by mysql:mysql. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.5 Ensure 'relay_log_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.relay_log_basename, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$b" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; case "$b" in /*) ;; *) b="$d/${b#./}" ;; esac; [ -d "$(dirname "$b")" ] || exit 1; n=$(find "$(dirname "$b")" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$(basename "$b").*" \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \) | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chmod 660 <relay_log_basename>.* && chown mysql:mysql <relay_log_basename>.*

title: Ensure 'general_log_file' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MySQL can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log (which can be encrypted), general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Passes when the general log is off and no old file remains, or when it is on and the file is -rw------- mysql:mysql. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.6 Ensure 'general_log_file' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; on=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.general_log + 0, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; f=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.general_log_file, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; if [ "$on" = 0 ]; then [ -e "$f" ] && echo "general log disabled but old file $f exists" || echo compliant; exit 0; fi; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ "$s" = "600 mysql mysql" ] && echo compliant || echo "$s"

remediation.command: Disable the general log (SET PERSIST general_log = OFF) and remove old general log files; if it must stay on: chmod 600 <general_log_file> && chown mysql:mysql <general_log_file>.

title: Ensure Example or Test Databases are Not Installed on Production Servers
description: The default MySQL installation does not contain any example or test databases. However, it is a good idea to review for common example databases and ensure they have been removed from production systems. Counts the common example databases (test, employees, world, world_x, sakila, airportdb, menagerie). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.2 Ensure Example or Test Databases are Not Installed on Production Servers

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME IN ('test','employees','world','world_x','sakila','airportdb','menagerie')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: DROP DATABASE <name>; for each example/test database on a production server.

title: Ensure 'allow-suspicious-udfs' is Set to 'OFF'
description: This option prevents attaching arbitrary shared library functions as user-defined functions by checking for at least one corresponding method named _init, _deinit, _reset, _clear, or _add. Counts allow-suspicious-udfs settings in the server option groups (my_print_defaults mysqld) and on the running server command line.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.3 Ensure 'allow-suspicious-udfs' is Set to 'OFF'

audit.command:
c=$(my_print_defaults mysqld 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(ps -eo comm=,args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=$( { printf '%s
' "$c"; printf '%s
' "$p" | awk '$1=="mysqld"||$1=="mariadbd"' | tr ' ' '
'; } | grep -Eic '^--allow[-_]suspicious[-_]udfs(=(1|on|true|yes))?$' ); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove allow-suspicious-udfs from the MySQL option files and from the server start-up command line, then restart.

title: Harden Usage for 'local_infile' on MySQL Clients
description: The local_infile parameter dictates whether files located on the MySQL client's computer can be loaded or selected via LOAD DATA INFILE or SELECT local_file. Checks the server-side branch of the benchmark (local_infile = 0); if LOAD DATA LOCAL is required, use clients 8.0.21+ with --load-data-local-dir and accept the finding as an exception. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.4 Harden Usage for 'local_infile' on MySQL Clients

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.local_infile = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST local_infile = 0"

title: Ensure Symbolic Links are Disabled
description: The symbolic-links and skip-symbolic-links options for MySQL determine whether symbolic link support is available. When use of symbolic links is enabled, they have different effects depending on the host platform. When symbolic links are disabled, then symbolic links stored in files or entries in tables are not used by the database. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.6 Ensure Symbolic Links are Disabled

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.have_symlink = 'DISABLED', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set skip-symbolic-links=YES under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf), then restart MySQL.

title: Ensure the 'secure_file_priv' is Configured Correctly
description: The secure_file_priv option restricts to paths used by LOAD DATA INFILE or SELECT local_file. It is recommended that this option be set to a file system location that contains only resources expected to be loaded by MySQL. Fails only when secure_file_priv is an empty string (import/export allowed everywhere). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.7 Ensure the 'secure_file_priv' is Configured Correctly

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.secure_file_priv IS NULL OR @@global.secure_file_priv <> '', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set secure_file_priv=<path_to_load_directory> (or remove the empty setting) under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf), then restart MySQL.

title: Use MySQL TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption
description: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) at-rest encryption protects your critical data by enabling data-at-rest encryption in the database. It protects the privacy of your information, prevents data breaches and helps meet regulatory requirements. Fails when any of audit_log_encryption (Enterprise only), binlog_encryption, innodb_redo_log_encrypt, innodb_undo_log_encrypt or table_encryption_privilege_check is OFF/NONE, or any InnoDB tablespace is unencrypted. Backup encryption is not checked. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.9 Use MySQL TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE VARIABLE_NAME IN ('audit_log_encryption','binlog_encryption','innodb_redo_log_encrypt','innodb_undo_log_encrypt','table_encryption_privilege_check') AND VARIABLE_VALUE IN ('OFF','NONE')) = 0 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.INNODB_TABLESPACES WHERE NAME NOT IN ('innodb_temporary','sys/sys_config') AND ENCRYPTION = 'N') = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Load a keyring component, then SET PERSIST table_encryption_privilege_check=ON, binlog_encryption=ON, innodb_redo_log_encrypt=ON, innodb_undo_log_encrypt=ON; set default_table_encryption=ON; ALTER TABLESPACE mysql ENCRYPTION='Y'; ALTER TABLE <t> ENCRYPTION='Y' (locks the table); encrypt audit logs and backups as well.

title: Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The PROCESS privilege found in the mysql.user table determines whether a given user can see statement execution information for all sessions.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.3 Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'PROCESS'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE PROCESS ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'SHUTDOWN' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The SHUTDOWN privilege simply enables use of the shutdown option to the mysqladmin command, which allows a user with the SHUTDOWN privilege the ability to shut down the MySQL server.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.5 Ensure 'SHUTDOWN' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'SHUTDOWN'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE SHUTDOWN ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'REPLICATION SLAVE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The REPLICATION SLAVE privilege governs whether a given user (in the context of the source server) can request updates that have been made on the source server.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.8 Ensure 'REPLICATION SLAVE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'REPLICATION SLAVE'; Ensure only accounts designated for replica users are returned.

remediation.command: REVOKE REPLICATION SLAVE ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure DML/DDL Grants are Limited to Specific Databases and Users
description: DML/DDL includes the set of privileges used to modify or create data structures. This includes INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, CREATE, and ALTER privileges.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.9 Ensure DML/DDL Grants are Limited to Specific Databases and Users

audit.command: Run SELECT User, Host, Db FROM mysql.db WHERE Select_priv='Y' OR Insert_priv='Y' OR Update_priv='Y' OR Delete_priv='Y' OR Create_priv='Y' OR Drop_priv='Y' OR Alter_priv='Y'; and ensure every returned user is permitted these privileges on the indicated database.

remediation.command: REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, ALTER ON <db>.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each unauthorized grant.

title: Securely Define Stored Procedures and Functions DEFINER and INVOKER
description: Stored procedure and stored function declarations include a definition of permissions which can be used to escalate permissions. It's important to inspect these settings to ensure they do not unnecessarily escalate privileges.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.10 Securely Define Stored Procedures and Functions DEFINER and INVOKER

audit.command: Run SHOW PROCEDURE STATUS; and SHOW FUNCTION STATUS; and inspect Definer and Security_type. For SQL SECURITY DEFINER routines owned by powerful users, review the code (SHOW CREATE PROCEDURE/FUNCTION <name>) and information_schema.routines/parameters.

remediation.command: Use SQL SECURITY INVOKER where possible, or set DEFINER to a least-privileged account (ALTER/CREATE ... DEFINER=...), and restrict EXECUTE on sensitive routines.

title: Ensure Proper Use Of 'SET_ANY_DEFINER'
description: Its critical to limit users ability to set and effective authorization ID that is used with executing a view or stored program. This grant provides a method to escalate privileges within MySQL views and procedures.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.11 Ensure Proper Use Of 'SET_ANY_DEFINER'

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'SET_ANY_DEFINER'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE SET_ANY_DEFINER ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure Proper Use Of ALLOW_NONEXISTENT_DEFINER
description: Its critical to limit users ability to set and effective authorization ID that is used with executing a view or stored program. This grant provides a method to escalate privileges within MySQL views and procedures.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.12 Ensure Proper Use Of ALLOW_NONEXISTENT_DEFINER

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'ALLOW_NONEXISTENT_DEFINER'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE ALLOW_NONEXISTENT_DEFINER ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'log_error' is configured correctly
description: The error log contains information about events such as mysqld starting and stopping, when a table needs to be checked or repaired, and, depending on the host operating system, stack traces when mysqld fails. Fails when log_error is empty, stderr or ./stderr.err. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 6.1 Ensure 'log_error' is configured correctly

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(IFNULL(@@global.log_error, '') NOT IN ('', 'stderr') AND @@global.log_error NOT LIKE '%stderr.err', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set log_error=<path to error log file> under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf), then restart MySQL.

title: Set 'default_password_lifetime' to Require a Yearly Password Change
description: Password expiry provides passwords with a time bounded lifetime. Passes when default_password_lifetime is between 1 and 365 days. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.4 Set 'default_password_lifetime' to Require a Yearly Password Change

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.default_password_lifetime BETWEEN 1 AND 365, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST default_password_lifetime = 365"

title: Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames
description: MySQL can make use of host wildcards when granting permissions to users on specific databases. For example, you may grant a given privilege to '<user>'@'%'. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 7.6 Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE host = '%'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: For each SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE host = '%' result: RENAME USER '<user>'@'%' TO '<user>'@'<specific host>'; or DROP USER.

title: Allowlist Approved Servers Belonging to a MySQL InnoDB Cluster
description: Optionally, specify an allowlist of approved servers that belong to the MySQL InnoDB Cluster.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 10.2 Allowlist Approved Servers Belonging to a MySQL InnoDB Cluster

audit.command: Run SELECT @@group_replication_ip_allowlist; on each InnoDB Cluster member. The value must list only the IPv4/IPv6 addresses, subnets or host names of approved cluster members (AUTOMATIC or overly broad ranges are a finding).

remediation.command: Set the allowlist on each member: STOP GROUP_REPLICATION; SET PERSIST group_replication_ip_allowlist = '<ip1>,<ip2>,<subnet>'; START GROUP_REPLICATION; (or ipAllowlist in MySQL Shell).

title: Place Databases on Non-System Partitions
description: It is generally accepted that host operating systems should include different filesystem partitions for different purposes. One set of filesystems is typically called system partitions, and these are generally reserved for host system/application operation.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1 Place Databases on Non-System Partitions

audit.command: Find the data and log locations: SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE (VARIABLE_NAME LIKE '%dir' OR VARIABLE_NAME LIKE '%file') AND VARIABLE_NAME NOT LIKE '%core%'; then run df -h <directory> for datadir and the others. They must not be on the root (/), /var or /usr partitions.

remediation.command: Create a dedicated partition/volume for the data, stop MySQL, move datadir there (copy preserving ownership mysql:mysql), update datadir in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf) and any SELinux/AppArmor policy, then start MySQL.

title: Disable MySQL Command History
description: On Linux/UNIX, the MySQL client and MySQL Shell log statements executed interactively to a history file. The default MySQL Client file is named .mysql_history in the user's home directory. The files are split by language and named history.sql, history.js and history.py. Most interactive commands run in the MySQL client application are saved to a history file. Run as root; counts client history files under /home and /root that are not symlinks to /dev/null.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.3 Disable MySQL Command History

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; l=$(find /home /root -maxdepth 4 \( -name .mysql_history -o -path '*/.mysqlsh/history*' \) 2>/dev/null); n=0; for x in $l; do [ "$(readlink "$x")" = /dev/null ] || n=$((n+1)); done; echo "$n"

remediation.guidance: For each user remove the history file and prevent re-creation: rm -f ~<user>/.mysql_history && ln -s /dev/null ~<user>/.mysql_history, or export MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null in the shell startup script; for MySQL Shell remove ~/.mysqlsh/history.* and run \option --persist history.autoSave=0.

title: Ensure MySQL is Run Under a Sandbox Environment
description: Use of the chroot() system call at startup, Systemd with settings to achieve isolation, or docker will put MySQL in a Sandbox environment.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.7 Ensure MySQL is Run Under a Sandbox Environment

audit.command: Check whether MySQL is confined: chroot option (grep -r '^chroot' /etc/mysql /etc/my.cnf*; must differ from datadir), systemd unit runs as a non-root user (systemctl status mysqld: Main PID not owned by root), or it runs in a container (docker ps / podman ps). None of these is a fail.

remediation.command: Run MySQL under systemd as the mysql user, in a container, or with chroot=<path> under [mysqld], and keep SELinux/AppArmor confinement enabled.

title: Backup of Configuration and Related Files
description: It is important to include configuration, log, key, certificates, and customized files in backups.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.6 Backup of Configuration and Related Files

audit.command: Check that the backup includes: edited configuration files (my.cnf and included files, mysqld-auto.cnf (SET PERSIST)), key management/keyring files, audit log files, SSL certificates and keys, UDF libraries and custom source code.

remediation.command: Add these configuration and related files to the backup set.

title: Dedicate the Machine Running MySQL
description: It is recommended that MySQL Server software be installed on a dedicated server. This architectural consideration affords flexibility in that the database server can be placed on a separate zone allowing access only from particular hosts and over particular protocols.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3 Dedicate the Machine Running MySQL

audit.command: Verify the host has no other roles and that no applications or services unrelated to MySQL are installed or running (systemctl list-units --type=service; package list).

remediation.command: Move unrelated services and applications off the MySQL host.

title: Do Not Reuse Usernames
description: Database user accounts should not be reused for multiple applications or users.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5 Do Not Reuse Usernames

audit.command: List accounts: SELECT host, user, plugin FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema','mysql.session','mysql.sys'); Each account must belong to exactly one system account, person or application; shared or reused usernames are a fail.

remediation.command: Create a separate account per person, application and system account, migrate their grants, and drop the shared accounts.

title: Require Current Password for Password Reset
description: Require the current password for password reset. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.9 Require Current Password for Password Reset

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.password_require_current = 1, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST password_require_current = ON"

title: Use Dual Passwords to Enable Higher Frequency Password Rotation
description: Dual passwords act as a tool to encourage password rotations in cases where a synchronized password change is not viable. By having a time delta to have old and new passwords in place, the process of replacing old passwords with new passwords within applications is simplified.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.10 Use Dual Passwords to Enable Higher Frequency Password Rotation

audit.command: Run SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE LENGTH(user_attributes->>'$.additional_password') > 0; An account that still has a secondary (dual) password after its password rotation has completed is a fail.

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' DISCARD OLD PASSWORD; once all clients use the new password.

title: Ensure AES Encryption Mode for AES_ENCRYPT/AES_DECRYPT is Configured Correctly
description: A block encryption mode with a Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode value and key length of 256 is recommended when using the AES_ENCRYPT() and AES_DECRYPT() functions for encryption. Passes for any aes-256-* mode (ecb, cbc, cfb1, cfb8, cfb128, ofb). Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.12 Ensure AES Encryption Mode for AES_ENCRYPT/AES_DECRYPT is Configured Correctly

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.block_encryption_mode LIKE 'aes-256-%', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set block_encryption_mode=aes-256-cbc under [mysqld] (or SET PERSIST block_encryption_mode = 'aes-256-cbc') after confirming applications that call AES_ENCRYPT/AES_DECRYPT pass the mode they need, then restart.

title: Ensure 'sql_mode' Contains 'STRICT_ALL_TABLES'
description: When data changing statements are made (i.e., INSERT, UPDATE), MySQL can handle invalid or missing values differently depending on whether strict SQL mode is enabled. When strict SQL mode is enabled, data may not be truncated or otherwise "adjusted" to make the data changing statement work. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.8 Ensure 'sql_mode' Contains 'STRICT_ALL_TABLES'

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(FIND_IN_SET('STRICT_ALL_TABLES', @@global.sql_mode) > 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Add STRICT_ALL_TABLES to sql_mode under [mysqld] (e.g. sql_mode=STRICT_ALL_TABLES,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION) after testing applications, then restart or SET GLOBAL sql_mode.

title: Ensure Log Files are Stored on a Non-System Partition
description: MySQL log files can be set in the MySQL configuration to exist anywhere on the filesystem. It is common practice to ensure that the system filesystem is left uncluttered by application logs. System filesystems include the root (/), /var, or /usr. Fails when log_bin_basename is under /var or /usr or on the root filesystem; passes when binary logging is off. Run on the database host. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 6.2 Ensure Log Files are Stored on a Non-System Partition

audit.command: d=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.log_bin_basename, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$b" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; case "$b" in /*) ;; *) b="$d/${b#./}" ;; esac; case "$b" in /var/*|/usr/*) echo "under /var or /usr: $b"; exit 0 ;; esac; m=$(df -P "$(dirname "$b")" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $6}'); [ -n "$m" ] || exit 1; [ "$m" = / ] && echo "on the root filesystem: $b" || echo compliant

remediation.command: Set log_bin=<path on a dedicated, non-system partition> under [mysqld] in /etc/my.cnf (or /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf), then restart MySQL.

title: Ensure 'log_error_verbosity' is Set to '2'
description: The log_error_verbosity system variable, set to 2 by default, specifies the verbosity of events sent to the MySQL error log. A value of 2 enables logging of error and warning messages, a value of 3 also includes informational logging, a value of 1 logs only errors. Runs mysql -NBe with the client defaults: put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600) or a mysql_config_editor login path, not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 6.3 Ensure 'log_error_verbosity' is Set to '2'

audit.command: out=$(mysql -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.log_error_verbosity = 2, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: mysql -e "SET PERSIST log_error_verbosity = 2"

title: Set Maximum Connection Limits for Server and per User
description: Limiting concurrent connections to a MySQL server can be used to reduce risk of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks performed by exhausting connection resources.
reference: CIS Oracle MySQL Community Server 8.4 Benchmark v1.1.0 - 8.3 Set Maximum Connection Limits for Server and per User

audit.command: Run SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_variables WHERE VARIABLE_NAME LIKE 'max_%connections'; (max_user_connections 0 = no limit) and SELECT user, host, max_user_connections FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT LIKE 'mysql.%' AND user <> 'root'; (0 = global value applies). No server or per-user limit is a fail.

remediation.command: Set max_connections and max_user_connections under [mysqld] (SET GLOBAL to apply now) and per account with ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' WITH MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS <n>;
